verdict.rationale: Metronome documents subscription lifecycle management that includes pricing changes. Changing a rate on the rate card moves every contract inheriting that rate card to the new price at the next billing period, which works as a crude all-at-once migration. The evidence never shows plan versioning, grandfathering existing subscribers on old prices, or targeted cohort migration. In fact, inheritance means every contract on that rate card moves together, and per-contract overrides would only be a workaround for grandfathering. Missing for 10: versioned plans, grandfathering of existing subscribers, cohort-targeted bulk migration tooling, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can change pricing without breaking existing subscribers — versioned plans, grandfathering, and bulk migration tools for moving cohorts to new prices

citations.quote: Use the Metronome API to manage your customer's subscription lifecycle including pricing changes, free trials, upgrades, and downgrades.
All contracts inherit the new pricing and customers are billed at the new rate at the start of the next billing period.
